questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design runtime-extensible routing logic for streaming with low-latency and backpressure concerns. Requires a registry for pluggable policies, a clean, minimal interface, and non-blocking paths to sinks. Examines tradeoffs between hot vs cold storage and observability.

## Key Concepts

- Strategy pattern
- Registry and runtime extensibility
- Backpressure and non-blocking IO
- Hot-swapping configuration

## Code Example

```ts
interface Message { source: string; schema: string; ttl: number }
interface Sink { enqueue(msg: Message): Promise<void> }
interface RoutingPolicy { selectSink(msg: Message): Sink }
class PolicyRegistry { register(name: string, policy: RoutingPolicy): void; get(name: string): RoutingPolicy | undefined }
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test hot-swapped policies without risking data loss?
- How do you ensure observability across multiple sinks when routing fails?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to extend behavior without touching core logic, a common real-world requirement in polyglot stacks.

## Key Concepts
- Decorator/Interceptor pattern
- Runtime registries and resolution order
- Idempotent wrapping and error propagation

## Code Example
```javascript
interface DAO<T> { get(id:string): Promise<T> }
interface Decorator<T> { (dao: DAO<T>): DAO<T> }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle decorator composition order and conflicts?
- How would you test the registry and wrapped DAOs with minimal mocks?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design extensible, runtime-modifiable tooling using common patterns.

## Key Concepts
- Command pattern, Registry, Factory, dynamic imports, plugin isolation
- Runtime extension without recompilation, error handling, help aggregation

## Code Example
```typescript
// Minimal interfaces
interface Command { execute(args: string[]): Promise<void> }
interface CommandFactory { create(): Command }
class CommandRegistry { register(name: string, factory: () => Command); resolve(name: string): Command; list(): string[] }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you sandbox/unload plugins, handle conflicting command names, and security concerns?
- How would you version plugins and roll back faulty ones?
